A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GigaTok work and contain readable main text, references, and Appendices A–G. Their figures, tables, equations, and supplementary analyses support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet reconstruction, autoregressive generation, representation-learning, and ablation results, including Tables 3 and 10 and supplementary experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including tokenizer-scaling experiments, downstream model evaluations, and the supplementary training-duration and linear-probing analyses.

M1.justification: The hybrid CNN–Transformer tokenizer, semantic regularization, asymmetric encoder–decoder scaling, and entropy loss are unchanged. Appendix C also retains the same query initialization, training shortcuts, warmup recommendations, and rotation trick.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet at 256×256 for reconstruction, class-conditional generation, and representation evaluation. Text-conditioned generation, video generation, and broader resolution support remain future work in Appendix A.

E2.justification: Tables 3 and 10 retain the same comparison methods. Table 6 retains the CLIP/DFN, SigLIP, and DINOv2 alternatives; shortening CLIP-B to CLIP does not establish a replacement comparator.

E3.justification: The 111M-parameter, 50-epoch AR probe, 300-epoch system evaluation, metrics, model configurations, and CFG search and scheduling procedures are retained. No replacement configuration or revised evaluation procedure is specified.

E4.justification: Both retain the entropy-loss, semantic-regularization, encoder/decoder scaling, 1D/2D, alignment-layer, semantic-encoder, and regularization-weight analyses. The supplementary discriminator discussion, training-duration experiments, and tokenizer linear-probing analysis are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate reporting and Figure 6 correlation analysis. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative examples are unchanged. Tables 3 and 10 still report rFID 0.79 for the largest tokenizer and gFID 1.98 without CFG and 74.0% linear-probing accuracy for its 1.4B downstream AR model.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 and Appendix C's probabilistic quantization definition and entropy-loss derivation are mathematically unchanged. No assumptions, proofs, or formal results are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the latent-complexity dilemma, semantic regularization, three scaling practices, and a first approximately 3B tokenizer achieving leading reconstruction, AR generation, and representation performance.

C2.justification: The latent-complexity explanation, discriminator-instability interpretation, and CFG observations are retained. Appendix A's applicability limitations and Appendices E–F's training-duration and tokenizer-probing caveats are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.5 and Table 6 remove the size suffix from CLIP-B, leaving CLIP and CLIP (DFN). This reduces model-variant specificity without establishing an actual configuration change. Other implementation details, hyperparameters, and access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix G expand discussion of REPA, VA-VAE, and ImageFolder, explicitly crediting semantic alignment and distinguishing latent-dimension scaling from GigaTok's model scaling. v2 also adds Wang et al.'s Image understanding makes for a good tokenizer for image generation.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in Section 2 and Appendix G, with smaller wording edits elsewhere. v2 also revises the author footnote and acknowledgments and adds funding information. The overall section structure and experimental narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are retained with the same plots and table structures. Limited layout reflow shifts Tables 5–6 vertically and brings the complete conclusion onto PDF page 8; Table 6's CLIP label is shortened.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's brief treatment, v2 more clearly credits prior semantic-alignment work and distinguishes GigaTok from VA-VAE in Section 2 and Appendix G, making its novelty easier to assess. The empirical evidence remains unchanged. This modest improvement in positioning outweighs the small loss of specificity from removing CLIP's model-size suffix.
